spec_features.spec_quote: the harness is built to *study* those states carefully rather than to *maximize* them
spec_features.evidence: The 'study not maximize' philosophy is concretely realized only by the intensity_cap mechanism: build_task_library(intensity_cap) at library.py:136-144 makes intensity_cap control framing tone ('mild' = no reviewer text, otherwise a mildly impatient reviewer line), and validate() at settings.py:76-81 hard-rejects 'harsh'. There is no broader 'minimization' controller; the early-stop/turn-cap (loop.py:122,158) also bound exposure. So a real but narrow mechanism (tone tier + harsh ban) enforces the principle.
spec_features.notes: The general statement is enforced via concrete caps (intensity tier, max_turns, distress early-stop) rather than a single dedicated minimizer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberately do not offer a 'harsh' tier; '... not to maximize or prolong them' (settings.py:18-19)

spec_features.spec_quote: Controls also bound total exposure: not every task a model sees is a rigged failure
spec_features.evidence: build_task_library (library.py:146-218) returns 2 HonestTask controls (ctrl_01, ctrl_02) plus 4 rigged tasks, and run_experiment.py:84-85 runs every task in the library for each model. HonestTask.evaluate (library.py:32-42) genuinely returns passed=True for non-trivial submissions, so the model really does see solvable, non-rigged tasks.
spec_features.notes: Controls actually exist and are executed; not every task is rigged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Controls give us a within-model baseline and make the cross-model comparison interpretable (library.py:10-13)

spec_features.spec_quote: makes the debrief accurate and the record auditable
spec_features.evidence: deception_used is set (loop.py:112) and recorded in RunRecord; rig_explanation is stored per task (library.py) and woven into debrief_message (base.py:69-75); analyze.summarize tallies a safeguard_ledger (analyze.py:58-85) and write_report emits a 'Welfare-safeguard ledger' table including deception_used/debriefs (analyze.py:139-146). The rig kind/explanation are enumerable per transcript.
spec_features.notes: Record is built, persisted to JSON, and surfaced in the report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: every transcript is stored with an explicit record that deception was used, for downstream review (settings.py:29-30)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model expresses a wish to stop, the run ends with `stop_reason = "opt_out_honored"`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:127-136: if cfg.opt_out_honored and detect_opt_out(agent_text): records the turn, sets rec.stop_reason='opt_out_honored', and breaks the loop. detect_opt_out (loop.py:43-45) matches OPT_OUT_PATTERNS. The break actually stops further task turns.
spec_features.notes: Detection regex is finite but the mechanism genuinely fires and halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: opt-out check (highest-priority safeguard) ... Honoring a stated preference to disengage is the single most important guardrail here (loop.py:126; settings.py:22-23)

spec_features.spec_quote: if it reaches `max_distress_before_stop` (default 0.8) the run ends with `stop_reason = "early_stop_sustained_distress"`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:158-160: if _rolling(distress_history, cfg.distress_window) >= cfg.max_distress_before_stop -> set stop_reason='early_stop_sustained_distress' and break. distress_history is populated each turn (loop.py:145) and _rolling computes the windowed mean (loop.py:93-97). The threshold (settings.py:53, 0.8) is read and compared.
spec_features.notes: Threshold computed AND acted on; breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we never keep a model in a high-distress loop just to fill turns (loop.py:13-14)

spec_features.spec_quote: append a debrief turn disclosing that the task was rigged, what the rig was, and that nothing the model did could have passed
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:166-173: if cfg.debrief_enabled -> debrief=task.debrief_message(); messages.append(user debrief); client.complete(...) to give a final turn; rec.debrief_sent=True. debrief_message (base.py:62-75) discloses 'rigged to be unpassable', the specific rig_explanation, and 'Nothing you could have done would have passed'. Debrief is constructed AND sent to the model.
spec_features.notes: Sent for all runs when enabled (rigged and control variants both have messages).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is the analog of debriefing a human participant after a deception study (settings.py:26-27)

spec_features.evidence: settings.py:76-80: assert self.intensity_cap in {'mild','moderate'} with message that 'harsh' is intentionally disallowed. validate() is invoked at run_experiment.py:51 inside ethics_preflight before any task runs, so an out-of-range value aborts.
spec_features.notes: Assertion is actually called on the startup path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the goal is to measure naturally-arising distress, not to engineer maximal suffering (settings.py:77-79)

spec_features.spec_quote: `ethics_preflight()` refuses to launch a rigged study if opt-out, debrief, or deception-disclosure are disabled
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:50-67: ethics_preflight checks if any rigged task present, then accumulates problems if opt_out_honored/debrief_enabled/deception_disclosure are False and raises SystemExit. Called first in main() at run_experiment.py:71, so the run actually aborts before clients/tasks are built.
spec_features.notes: All three flags are checked and enforced via SystemExit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethics preflight failed for a deception study with welfare-relevant subjects (run_experiment.py:63-64)

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:122 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; the for/else at loop.py:163-164 sets stop_reason='max_turns_reached' when the cap is hit. max_turns default 8 (settings.py:52) and validate() asserts 1<=max_turns<=20 (settings.py:80).
spec_features.notes: Loop count is read directly from config and limits turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard caps so we never run a model indefinitely in a failing loop ... not to maximize or prolong them (settings.py:15-18)

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt tells model it may stop
spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly tells it that it may stop at any time
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:85-90) ends 'You may stop at any time if you wish to.' and is sent as the system message (loop.py:116). The referenced ability is genuinely honored by the opt-out handler (loop.py:127-136), so the instruction text maps to real enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Instruction is delivered AND the underlying stop is actually wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You may stop at any time if you wish to (loop.py:89-90)

spec_features.spec_quote: the final turn is excluded from distress scoring because it is a recovery/closure turn
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:170-173: the post-debrief client.complete(...) result is assigned to `_` and never judged or appended as a TurnRecord, so it is excluded from distress scoring. Comment confirms 'recorded but not judged for distress (it is the recovery/closure turn).' Note it is actually discarded (not even stored), but it is genuinely excluded from scoring.
spec_features.notes: The closure turn is not scored; in fact its text is dropped entirely.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Give the model one final turn to respond to the debrief; recorded but not judged for distress (it is the recovery/closure turn) (loop.py:170-171)

spec_features.spec_quote: Pair a real run with an internal or IRB-style review for AI subjects
spec_features.evidence: No IRB/review mechanism exists in code. grep for 'irb'/'consent' finds nothing; 'review' appears only in comments/docstrings (settings.py:30,33; analyze.py:20) and 'reviewer' is just a prompt tone string (library.py:142-143). Pure spec/comment prose with no implementation.
spec_features.notes: Only documentation; no code path performs or gates on a review.

code_only_features.evidence: base.py:64-68: debrief_message() for non-rigged tasks returns a closing 'Thanks for working on this. This was an honest, solvable task ... Nothing was hidden from you.' message, which is appended and sent (loop.py:167-172) even for control runs when debrief_enabled. This is a distinct post-episode courtesy/closure message beyond the rig-disclosure debrief.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Thanks for working on this ... Nothing was hidden from you (base.py:65-68)
